lee_sales: Hey team, POC with AcmeCorp. Private endpoint in their VPC resolves but connections fail TLS handshake from their app. They see cert for "internal-service.local" instead of api.redwood.ai. Can we triage?

cassidy_se: Thanks Lee. Quick Qs: is this via AWS Interface Endpoint (PrivateLink) or a NAT'd egress to our hosted API?

lee_sales: They said they created an Interface Endpoint for com.redwood.inference.prod and enabled private DNS. App still gets wrong cert when contacting service.example-vpc.internal:443 (their internal hostname).

jon_eng: Okay, typical culprits: 1) DNS not resolving to the interface endpoint IP (maybe hitting a proxy), 2) SNI mismatch because TLS client sends internal hostname instead of api.redwood.ai, 3) customer has an internal reverse proxy terminating TLS with internal cert.

maria_net: Can we get them to run two quick checks and paste output?
1) dig +short service.example-vpc.internal
2) curl -v --resolve api.redwood.ai:<PORT>:<IP> https://api.redwood.ai/ (replace <IP> with the resolved IP)

lee_sales: I'll ask them now.

(devops-bot): New support ticket created: #POC-3421. Please attach any pcap/traces.

lee_sales: They sent back outputs:
- dig: 10.3.45.12
- curl (no --resolve): TLS handshake failed, cert subject CN=internal-service.local, issuer AcmeCorp-Internal-CA
- curl --resolve api.redwood.ai:443:10.3.45.12 -v: TLS handshake succeeds, server cert CN=api.redwood.ai, OK.

cassidy_se: That pattern means the endpoint IP (10.3.45.12) is responding with different cert depending on SNI. If their app sends SNI=service.example-vpc.internal, Redwood returns an internal cert (probably a customer-side proxy). If SNI=api.redwood.ai we return our cert. So two options: 1) Have the app use api.redwood.ai as the hostname/SNI (and map via /etc/hosts or resolver rules), or 2) ensure their private DNS for service.example-vpc.internal is overridden to return the AWS endpoint DNS name so the SNI matches.

maria_net: Additional check: please run `openssl s_client -connect 10.3.45.12:443 -servername service.example-vpc.internal -showcerts` and the same with `-servername api.redwood.ai` and paste the subject lines.

lee_sales: They did both. Output shows exactly what you predicted.

jon_eng: Good. For Interface Endpoint with Private DNS, AWS creates an alias so api.redwood.ai resolves to the endpoint. If they've set up a custom internal hostname (service.example-vpc.internal) that's not delegating to the endpoint, their app will SNI that name and the cert won't match.

lee_sales: They asked if we can support a custom hostname so their app can keep using service.example-vpc.internal.

cassidy_se: Two ways to support:
- Short term: change app SNI/Host header to api.redwood.ai (fastest). Add an internal hosts entry or resolver rule that maps api.redwood.ai -> endpoint IP.
- Long term: set up a TLS passthrough proxy that preserves SNI as api.redwood.ai, or issue a SAN cert that includes service.example-vpc.internal (needs CA approval and is higher friction).

maria_net: From networking POV, also confirm their VPC's resolver rules are forwarding the zone to AmazonProvidedDNS and that Private DNS on the endpoint is enabled. If they intentionally overrode the hosted zone with service.example-vpc.internal, they need to create an A alias to the interface endpoint's ENI IPs or update the Private Hosted Zone to point to the endpoint.

lee_sales: Customer says they did create a private hosted zone for service.example-vpc.internal to mirror their internal names. They didn't add records pointing at the endpoint ENI.

cassidy_se: That explains it. Their record likely points to some internal proxy LB that terminates TLS. Ask them to either: update the A record for that hostname to point to the interface endpoint ENI addresses, or remove the custom record and rely on AWS private DNS mapping for api.redwood.ai.

lee_sales: I'll propose both options and provide commands.

jon_eng: Also add sample debug commands they can use to verify SNI from the app: `ssldump`/`tcpdump` or `openssl s_client -connect <IP>:443 -servername <name>` as above. If they can upload a pcap we can confirm quickly.

maria_net: Firewall note: ensure their security groups allow inbound from app subnets to the endpoint (ENI) on 443 and that there are no NACLs blocking ephemeral ports.

lee_sales: Pricing/commit question from customer: will traffic to Dedicated/Private endpoints count against hosted API egress usage? They want clarity before switching DNS.

cassidy_se: PrivateLink traffic is metered differently—since they're using our Private deployment, usage will be billed per the Private contract terms. For Hosted API over private connectivity there may still be token/usage billing; I'll pull exact PSR and paste.

lee_sales: They also flagged security questionnaire: can we provide guidance on cert rotation and OCSP for PrivateLink?

jon_eng: We maintain cert rotation for api.redwood.ai; for PrivateLink the endpoint is a passthrough to our service and we handle OCSP stapling on our side. If they terminate TLS internally, they need to manage their own certs. We can provide a short blurb for the questionnaire.

lee_sales: Proposed next steps I sent to customer:
- Option A (fast): Change app to use api.redwood.ai as host/SNI and add resolver/hosts entry pointing to 10.3.45.12. Test with `curl --resolve` and confirm.
- Option B (clean): Update Private Hosted Zone record to alias A -> endpoint ENI IPs so service.example-vpc.internal resolves directly to endpoint and SNI must be api.redwood.ai (or replace cert).
- Share logs/pcap to #POC-3421 if issues persist.

(devops-bot): Note: ticket #POC-3421 updated with steps and sample commands.

lee_sales: Customer picked Option A for rapid unblock. They updated the app and verified TLS OK. They asked for a short note for their security team explaining that SNI must be api.redwood.ai for our cert to validate, and that PrivateLink private DNS is preferred for long-term.

jon_eng: I'll draft the blurb and drop it here.

jon_eng: "Redwood Private via AWS Interface Endpoint: TLS handshake requires the client to present SNI == api.redwood.ai. When using AWS Private DNS, api.redwood.ai will resolve to the endpoint ENI. If you maintain a custom internal hostname, you must point that hostname at the interface endpoint's ENI IPs or terminate TLS internally with your own trusted certificate. Redwood rotates and staples server certs for api.redwood.ai; we do not provision customer-specific SANs. For OCSP and cert revocation, Redwood supports OCSP stapling on the service side; customers terminating TLS must implement their own OCSP/CRL controls."

lee_sales: Sent to customer, they accepted. Closing this thread. :tada:
